🌍 Learning

Generalisation

In simple words

A model's ability to work well on new examples it has never seen, not just on its training data.

A model's ability to do well on new examples, not just on the ones it was trained on. Generalisation is the real goal of machine learning: a model that only remembers its training data is overfitting.

Example. A student who understands how to solve equations can solve new ones in a test. A student who memorised the answers to the textbook exercises can't — that's the difference between generalising and overfitting.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 2: Machine Learning

Related words

  • OverfittingWhen a model memorises its training examples so closely that it does badly on new data.
  • Data augmentationMaking more training examples from the ones you have, for example by flipping, turning or shifting pictures.
  • ModelA program that has learned patterns from data and uses them to make predictions or create something new.
  • Test setExamples put aside before training and used only to check how well a model does on data it has never seen.
